clue.text: Kangaroo eating large loaf

indicators.note: the kangaroo word takes the large abbreviation into its middle, as if consuming it

parts.note: a boomer is Australian slang for a large male kangaroo
L is the standard clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A kangaroo tucks into a big loaf of bread.
explanation.walkthrough: BOOMER (an Australian word for a big male kangaroo) takes in L after its first letter. A bloomer is a British crusty white loaf with diagonal slashes across the top.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is a type of large crusty white bread loaf with a slashed top.

clue.text: Not the top grade old game, "Smashed"

parts.note: B is the grade below the top grade of A
lotto is an old game of chance like bingo

explanation.surface: A second-rate old game has been smashed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smashed' is slang for drunk, not broken.
explanation.definitionFit: Blotto is British slang for very drunk.

clue.text: In Brno it powered back the freedom to choose

indicators.note: back tells us the hidden letters are read in reverse
the letters are found within the run of words

explanation.surface: Something in the Czech city of Brno drove the liberty of choice backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'brNO IT POwered' from right to left. Brno is a city in the Czech Republic.
explanation.definitionFit: An option is a choice, or the right to choose between alternatives.

clue.text: Short duration composition of Britten with a 1 across

parts.note: mo is short for moment, a brief time

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A brief piece by Benjamin Britten is accompanied by a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition of' rearranges BRITTEN and A into NTBRETIA. Britten suggests a composer; here it is just letters. 1 across is a bloomer, a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Montbretia is a garden plant with sprays of orange-red flowers, a bloomer in the flowering sense.

clue.text: Bullet heat

definitions.meaning: a single shot or cartridge of ammunition
a qualifying stage in a sports competition

explanation.definitionFit: A round is a single bullet and also a stage of a competition, as is a heat.

clue.text: Storyteller? First, be mobile

indicators.note: mobile means able to move about, so the letters of the two words shift into a new order

explanation.surface: A request that a storyteller should first be on the move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mobile' rearranges the seven letters of FIRST BE. The question mark warns that 'Storyteller' is meant in its jokey sense of a teller of untruths, not an author.
explanation.definitionFit: A teller of stories in the playful sense is a liar, someone who tells small fibs.

clue.text: Cut it fine cooking pasta

indicators.note: cooking means the letters are being prepared and mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone leaves it to the last minute while making pasta.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' rearranges the letters of CUT IT FINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Fettucini are long flat ribbons of pasta, also spelt fettuccine.

clue.text: 1 across's word to surprise Black

parts.note: boo is the exclamation used to startle someone

explanation.surface: Someone startles a man called Black with a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after '1 across' is 'is'. Here 1 across is a bloomer in the sense of a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A boob is British slang for a silly mistake, the same as a bloomer.

clue.text: Water disturbance: boron covered by miniature one in drainpipes?

indicators.note: the water word and boron are enclosed by the miniature word

parts.note: a toy is a miniature version, as in a toy dog
an eddy is a swirl in water
B is the chemical symbol for boron

explanation.surface: Disturbed water and a chemical element are found inside a drainpipe.
explanation.walkthrough: EDDYB goes inside TOY after its T. Drainpipes are tight narrow trousers, worn by Teddy boys, 1950s British youths in Edwardian-style dress.
explanation.definitionFit: Teddy boys of the 1950s wore drainpipe trousers, so one is someone dressed in drainpipes.

clue.text: "Kidnapped" then ____ , given Swallows and Amazons treatment?

definitions.text: "Kidnapped" then ____ , given Swallows and Amazons treatment?

parts.words: "Kidnapped" then ____ , given Swallows and Amazons treatment?
parts.note: kidnap victims are later bought back; also the author of Swallows and Amazons, Arthur Ransome, makes a verb, as if given his treatment

explanation.walkthrough: Kidnapped is also a Robert Louis Stevenson novel, which fits the bookish second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: To be freed by payment after a kidnap is the next step, and it also puns on Arthur Ransome's name.

clue.text: A lot of bag is back-to-front

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: back-to-front means the word for bag is written in reverse order

parts.note: to bag a fish or prize is to net it

explanation.surface: Part of a bag has been put on the wrong way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of bag' reads as a portion of the bag, but 'A lot' alone is the definition and 'is back-to-front' turns only the bag word.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something a lot means doing it frequently, many times over.

clue.text: Blunt rod, dense at the centre, like an overgrown path?

indicators.note: the answer sits in the middle of the run of words, with outer letters left off each end

explanation.surface: A blunt rod with a dense core is compared to a path gone wild.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop BL from the front and SE from the end of the words and the answer runs through what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A path grown over with weeds has clearly not been walked on by anyone for a long time.

clue.text: Gold's back in Bath, a grim old entertainer

indicators.note: the reversed gold word is placed inside the bath word

parts.note: a tub is a bath

indicators.note: back means the heraldic word for gold is read in reverse

parts.note: OR is gold in heraldry; the 's is a link
taken as written
dour means grim or severe

explanation.surface: Gold has returned to the city of Bath, where an elderly performer looks grim.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath with its capital looks like the English spa city, but here it is just an ordinary tub; 'back' turns the heraldic gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Troubadours were medieval poet-musicians who travelled and performed songs of courtly love.

clue.text: 1 across has a role in party politics

indicators.note: the answer plays a part within the two words, its letters sitting across their junction

explanation.surface: A mistake plays its part in party politics.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the two words: the end of 'party' and the start of 'politics'. Here 1 across is read as a bloomer in the sense of a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A misprint in typed or printed text is a small mistake, a blunder in British slang.

clue.text: Head studying irregular polygon holding her ground

indicators.note: the rearranged shape word contains the other rearranged word
irregular means out of order, so the letters of the shape word are mixed
ground means crushed and broken up, so the letters of her are rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd-shaped figure contains her piece of land.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate anagram signals work here: 'irregular' on the shape word and 'ground' on the pronoun, with 'holding' putting one inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrenology was the Victorian pseudoscience of reading character from bumps on the skull.

clue.text: Beauty of a certain country's language enhanced by 1 across

indicators.note: enhanced by means added to, so the flower follows the language

parts.note: the language of England is English
1 across is a bloomer, a flower, and a rose is one

explanation.surface: A national tongue is improved by the addition of a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 1 across is a bloomer in the sense of a plant that flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes a fair-skinned, classically pretty English woman, a recognised beauty type.

clue.text: Working outside, not quite the millionaire but striving to be one?

indicators.note: the working word goes round the other piece

parts.note: a machine that is going is working

indicators.note: not quite means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: J. Paul Getty was a famously rich American oil tycoon

explanation.surface: Working outside, someone is not quite a millionaire yet but aims to be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striving to be one?' means striving to be a millionaire; 'not quite' trims the tycoon's surname and 'outside' wraps the working word round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Go-getting means ambitious and energetic, as someone keen to make a fortune would be.

clue.text: Provide residential care in Soho (uses itemised)

indicators.note: the answer is found within the following words

explanation.surface: Someone in London's Soho uses an itemised bill for residential care.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'soHO USES ITemised'. Soho is a district of central London.
explanation.definitionFit: To house-sit is to live in and look after someone's home while they are away.

clue.text: Descent of awful dirge into tinkle

indicators.note: the rearranged song goes inside the word for tinkle

parts.note: tinkle and pee are both slang for urinating

indicators.note: awful means badly done, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dreadful funeral song descends into a tinkling sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tinkle' looks like a bell's sound but is childish slang for urinating; 'awful' scrambles the funeral song before 'into' places it.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedigree is a line of descent or ancestry.

clue.text: How long it takes to remove lid, maybe, when a jar becomes available?

definitions.text: How long it takes to remove lid, maybe
definitions.meaning: the time taken to get something such as a lid or tin open
a jar is British slang for a glass of beer, served once a pub unlocks its doors

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain pubs traditionally opened only at fixed hours, so the moment they opened was when a drink could first be bought.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both the duration of opening something and the hour a pub starts serving.

clue.text: See 25
Concert introduces first sign of strain to marriage

indicators.note: the marriage word takes in a letter, bringing it inside

parts.note: a union is a marriage

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A concert brings the first strain into a marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Concert' is agreement here, as in acting in concert, not a musical event.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in concert means acting in agreement or harmony, together as one.

clue.text: A 1 across, though not, say, Daisy, is still a 1 across

indicators.note: though not tells us to take away the cow word from the flower name

parts.note: 1 across is a bloomer, a flowering plant, and the cowslip is one
Daisy is a traditional name for a cow; 'say' marks it as an example

explanation.surface: A flower other than a daisy is still a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests Daisy is a flower; she is a cow. Take COW from COWSLIP and what remains is a bloomer in the other sense, a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip is a small mistake, which a bloomer is in British slang.

clue.text: Stationer relocated: just fifth of business booming

indicators.note: relocated means moved to a new place, so the letters of the word go into a new order
only the fifth letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A stationer's shop has moved, and only part of the business is thriving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relocated' scrambles the shop owner's word; 'just fifth of business' supplies its fifth letter, an N, at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Stentor was a herald in Greek legend with a huge voice, so the word describes a loud, booming voice.

clue.text: Close on temperature for a usually colder period

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: nigh means near or close

explanation.surface: Something close to a temperature for a usually colder period.
explanation.definitionFit: Night-time is typically cooler than the day, after the sun has set.

clue.text: Not for one getting over sex

parts.note: an means one, as in a or an

indicators.note: getting over is read as being turned over, so the word for sex is reversed

parts.note: it is slang for sex or sex appeal

explanation.surface: Someone opposes one getting over sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting over' is read as being turned over, a reversal signal; 'it' for sex appeal is an old convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti means opposed to, the opposite of being for something.

clue.text: Analyst in good 1 across one reserved

parts.note: a shrink is slang for a psychoanalyst
taken as written
1 across is a bloomer, a flower, and the violet is one

explanation.surface: A psychoanalyst sits in a pleasant flower bed with a reserved person.
explanation.walkthrough: Here 1 across is read as a bloomer, a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes a shy, timid person who avoids attention.

clue.text: Goblins don't need black looks

indicators.note: not needing something means doing without it, so the black letter is removed

parts.note: bogles are goblins or bogeymen in Scottish and northern English folklore
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Goblins can manage without the colour black.
explanation.walkthrough: Take B from BOGLES. 'Goblins' cannot lose a B to give the answer; it must first become its synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogles are leering or lingering looks, often amorous ones.

clue.text: Crawling, getting ready to drive around unnumbered motorway

indicators.note: the golf word wraps itself round the motorway letter

parts.note: in golf, teeing up means placing the ball on a tee before driving it
M stands for motorway; British motorways are numbered (M1, M25), so a bare M has no number

explanation.surface: A golfer prepares to tee off near a motorway with no number.
explanation.walkthrough: TEEING takes M inside to give TEEMING. 'Crawling' means swarming with, as in 'crawling with ants'.
explanation.definitionFit: A place crawling with something is teeming with it, packed full and swarming.

clue.text: Don to see what can be got away with

definitions.meaning: to don clothes is to put them on, as when testing a garment for size

definitions.text: to see what can be got away with
definitions.meaning: to test someone's limits by acting cheekily

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both testing clothes for fit and chancing one's luck to test limits.
